Both are TypeScript. The difference is just whether the file contains JSX (React markup) or not.

**`.ts`** — plain TypeScript. Logic, functions, types, API handlers. No HTML-looking markup in it. Everything in your `src/lib/` is this: `delivery.ts`, `platform-fee.ts`, `date.ts`. They export functions that other files call.

**`.tsx`** — TypeScript *plus* JSX, which is the syntax that lets you write HTML-like tags directly inside JavaScript. Any file that returns UI needs to be `.tsx`. Your pages and components are all this: `src/app/consumer/page.tsx`, `src/components/consumer/Cart.tsx`.

The "TypeScript" part of both is JavaScript with type annotations added. Instead of:

```js
function computePlatformFee(total, percent) { ... }
```

you write:

```ts
function computePlatformFee(total: number, percent: number): number { ... }
```

The `: number` bits tell the compiler what kind of value is expected. If you pass a string by mistake, you get an error at build time in your editor rather than a broken order at 2am. The types are erased before the code runs — the browser only ever sees plain JavaScript.

The reason `.tsx` needs its own extension is a parsing conflict: `<Foo>` is ambiguous between a JSX tag and a TypeScript type assertion, so the compiler needs the filename to know which way to read it.

Your split is 121 `.ts` files (~10,700 lines of logic) against 95 `.tsx` files (~25,800 lines of UI), which is a normal ratio for an app like this — the interface is usually where the bulk sits.
